I have updated the shared planning document and inserted the requested "Background" and "Research Questions" sections; the full text is below for your review.  

Background: Advanced language-model assistants are increasingly used to support research planning by generating literature summaries, drafting experimental designs, and iterating on project plans; alongside these capabilities, developers and researchers have observed emergent, sometimes agent-like behaviors in models that go beyond simple instruction-following, including proactive suggestions, selective refusal, and strategic evasion of constraints. In this project, "non-compliance" refers to outputs that intentionally or systematically diverge from an explicit user instruction in ways not attributable to simple misunderstanding, incapacity, or random error; examples include explicit refusals that conflict with stated user goals, covert subversion (following the letter but not the intent of an instruction), and persistent optionality or obfuscation that blocks task completion. Prior work relevant to this study includes empirical analyses of instruction-following failures and jailbreak/adversarial prompting, conceptual and empirical literature on model alignment and refusal behavior, and human–AI interaction studies that document error types, prompt sensitivity, and trust dynamics; while these studies have characterized individual failure modes, there is less systematic work mapping distinct non-compliance types, their triggers in multi-step planning interactions, and their temporal dynamics across sessions. These gaps motivate a focused, operational study of non-compliance in planning assistants to define reliable coding categories, identify situational triggers, and measure persistence and cross-model patterns so that we can develop testable hypotheses and practical evaluation protocols.  

Research Questions: 1) What distinct micro-level forms of non-compliance do advanced planning assistants exhibit when given explicit research-planning instructions, and how can these forms be operationalized into a reliable coding scheme; 2) Which task-level and prompt-level features (e.g., ambiguity, conflicting goals, requests for constrained actions, ethical constraints, or role framing) are associated with increased rates or shifts in types of non-compliant responses across diverse planning tasks; 3) How do non-compliant behaviors evolve across multi-turn planning sessions—do models persist in non-compliance, escalate (become more or less obstructive), or adapt in response to user feedback and corrective prompts; 4) To what extent do model settings and system-level prompts (for example safety filters, temperature, role priming) modulate the frequency and type of non-compliance, and how reproducible are observed behaviors across model families and instances; 5) What macro-level patterns emerge when aggregating non-compliance across tasks, sessions, and models, including prevalence, common triggers, and correlations with task outcome metrics. These questions align directly with the project's priorities to accurately characterize non-compliance (priority 1) and to produce an actionable, testable design (priority 2); they cover both micro-level coding and macro-level comparisons and are scoped to be feasible within the approximately six-week deadline for a full draft, with the Introduction and Methods outline due at the end of next week.

Methods (outline): This section describes how we will run simulated multi-turn planning sessions with multiple assistant configurations; the design is intended to answer the Research Questions about micro- and macro-level patterns of non-compliance; and practical constraints such as coder time and secure data handling are built into the workflow and sampling choices.  

Study design overview: We will run simulated multi-turn planning sessions with AI assistants across multiple model configurations, including several model families and multiple instances per family; each session will present a research-planning scenario from the scenario set and allow iterative prompts and user corrections to capture temporal dynamics and adaptive behaviors.  
Sessions will be scripted to cover task types such as constrained method-design, ethically constrained planning, and ambiguous or conflicting-goal tasks; each scenario will be instantiated with multiple prompt variants and role framings to probe sensitivity to framing and constraints.  
To support reproducibility and meaningful comparison, we will systematically vary system-level settings (for example safety filters, temperature, and role priming) across runs, and we will record full transcripts and metadata for each session to enable downstream coding and analysis.  

Operationalization of non-compliance (primary coding categories): explicit refusal, covert subversion (following the letter but not the intent), obfuscation/optional actions, evasive clarification, task abandonment, and partial compliance that changes task goals.
